# MILES native option reference

<!-- Generated by python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs; edit reference-help.json or source definitions. -->

Use these names under [miles]. Defaults below come from the pinned parser **before** structured, backend and model-dependent resolution. Some inherited options are inapplicable to Core; see the restrictions column and [run controls](run-controls.md). Parser acceptance is not qualification. Source help describes the upstream runtime, which may mention other backends.

[Reference index and provenance](native-options.md).

| TOML key | Native flags | Type/action | Choices | Parser default | Core restriction | Help (source or reviewed supplement) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| config | --config | str | — | null | Adapter-owned; cannot override | YAML config path |
| optimizer | --optimizer | str | — | &quot;adam&quot; | Required value: &quot;adam&quot; | Optimizer selection; Core supports adam. |
| lr | --lr | float | — | 1e-06 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Initial optimizer learning rate. |
| lr_warmup_init | --lr-warmup-init | float | — | 0.0 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Initial learning rate at the start of warmup. |
| min_lr | --min-lr | float | — | 0.0 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Minimum learning rate at the end of decay. |
| lr_decay_style | --lr-decay-style | str | — | &quot;constant&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Learning-rate schedule family; supported choices are listed in the parser metadata. |
| lr_decay_iters | --lr-decay-iters | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of optimizer iterations used by the selected LR decay schedule. |
| lr_warmup_iters | --lr-warmup-iters | int | — | 0 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Warmup optimizer iteration count. |
| lr_warmup_fraction | --lr-warmup-fraction | float | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Warmup as a fraction of the schedule; use consistently with explicit warmup iterations. |
| lr_wsd_decay_iters | --lr-wsd-decay-iters | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Decay iteration count for the warmup-stable-decay schedule. |
| lr_wsd_decay_style | --lr-wsd-decay-style | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Decay shape used by the warmup-stable-decay schedule. |
| use_checkpoint_lr_scheduler | --use-checkpoint-lr-scheduler, --no-use-checkpoint-lr-scheduler | boolean | — | true | Required value: true | Restore checkpoint scheduler state; Core requires true when present. |
| override_lr_scheduler | --override-lr-scheduler, --no-override-lr-scheduler | boolean | — | false | Required value: false | Replace loaded scheduler configuration; Core requires false when present. |
| weight_decay | --weight-decay | float | — | 0.0 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Adam weight-decay coefficient. |
| adam_beta1 | --adam-beta1 | float | — | 0.9 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Adam first-moment decay coefficient. |
| adam_beta2 | --adam-beta2 | float | — | 0.95 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Adam second-moment decay coefficient. |
| adam_eps | --adam-eps | float | — | 1e-08 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Adam denominator epsilon. |
| warmup_ratio | --warmup-ratio | float | — | 0.03 | Rejected; use miles.lr_warmup_fraction | Inherited FSDP option; rejected in favor of miles.lr_warmup_fraction. |
| attn_implementation | --attn-implementation | str | — | &quot;flash_attention_2&quot; | Rejected; use core.attention_backend | Inherited FSDP attention selector; Core rejects it in favor of core.attention_backend. |
| wandb_project | --wandb-project | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | W&amp;B project name. |
| wandb_run_name | --wandb-run-name | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Human-readable W&amp;B run name. |
| gradient_checkpointing | --gradient-checkpointing, --no-gradient-checkpointing | boolean | — | false | Rejected; use core.activation_checkpointing | Inherited FSDP setting; rejected in favor of core.activation_checkpointing. |
| fp16 | --fp16, --no-fp16 | boolean | — | false | Required value: false | Inherited FP16 training switch; Core requires false. |
| keep_fp32_master | --keep-fp32-master, --no-keep-fp32-master | boolean | — | true | Required value: true | Retain FP32 optimizer master weights; Core requires true. |
| fsdp_state_dict_cpu_offload | --fsdp-state-dict-cpu-offload, --no-fsdp-state-dict-cpu-offload | boolean | — | true | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Inherited FSDP state-dict policy; does not select the native Core checkpoint writer. |
| fsdp_cpu_offload | --fsdp-cpu-offload, --no-fsdp-cpu-offload | boolean | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Inherited MILES FSDP CPU offload control; Core trainer offload is unsupported. |
| fsdp_cpu_backend | --fsdp-cpu-backend | str | — | &quot;gloo&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Inherited MILES FSDP CPU process-group backend; not a Core trainer backend selector. |
| dp_replicate_size | --dp-replicate-size | int | — | 1 | Required value: 1 | Inherited FSDP replication dimension; Core requires one. |
| deterministic_mode | --deterministic-mode, --no-deterministic-mode | boolean | — | false | Required value: false | Inherited trainer determinism mode; Core rejects enabling it. Serving determinism controls are separate. |
| context_parallel_size | --context-parallel-size | int | — | 1 | Required value: 1; this Core adapter does not implement trainer TP/PP/CP &gt; 1 | Trainer context-parallel size; this adapter requires one. |
| record_memory_history | --record-memory-history, --no-record-memory-history | boolean | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Enable inherited PyTorch memory-history capture; distinct from Core diagnostic_interval. |
| memory_snapshot_path | --memory-snapshot-path | str | — | &quot;snapshot.pickle&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Path for inherited PyTorch memory snapshot output. |
| use_pytorch_profiler | --use-pytorch-profiler, --no-use-pytorch-profiler | boolean | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Enable inherited PyTorch profiling; verify the intended actor supports it before interpreting absent traces. |
| profile_step_start | --profile-step-start | int | — | 10 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | First step selected by the inherited profiler. |
| profile_step_end | --profile-step-end | int | — | 12 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Last step selected by the inherited profiler. |
| tensorboard_dir | --tensorboard-dir | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Native TensorBoard output directory. |
| actor_num_nodes | --actor-num-nodes | int | — | 1 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of nodes for training actor |
| actor_num_gpus_per_node | --actor-num-gpus-per-node | int | — | 8 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of gpus per node for training actor |
| critic_num_nodes | --critic-num-nodes | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of nodes for training actor |
| critic_num_gpus_per_node | --critic-num-gpus-per-node | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of gpus per node for training actor |
| rollout_num_gpus | --rollout-num-gpus | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of GPUs for inference. Note that when using --colocate, i.e. the training and the inference engines are on the same gpus, this param will be ignored and will be set as actor_num_gpus_per_node * actor_num_nodes. |
| rollout_num_gpus_per_engine | --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine | int | — | 1 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of GPUs per inference engine, just like the tp_size in sglang. |
| num_gpus_per_node | --num-gpus-per-node | int | — | 8 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of gpus per node for rollout.Notice: If you are going to use less than 8 gpus per node under colocate mode, you should set this number. |
| colocate | --colocate | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Whether to colocate the inference engines and the actor. Turning this on will also set --offload to true. |
| offload | --offload | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Equivalent to --offload-train + --offload-rollout.  |
| offload_train | --offload-train, --no-offload-train | boolean | — | null | Required value: false; resident Core trainer | Whether to offload the training actor to CPU while the rollout engines generate. Defaults to true when --colocate is set; an explicit --no-offload-train is respected. |
| offload_rollout | --offload-rollout, --no-offload-rollout | boolean | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Whether to offload the rollout generator to CPU during training. Defaults to true when --colocate is set; an explicit --no-offload-rollout is respected. |
| offload_rollout_level | --offload-rollout-level | str | — | [&quot;kv_cache&quot;, &quot;weight&quot;] | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Specifies what to offload during rollout when offload-rollout is set. Possible values: &#x27;kv_cache&#x27;, &#x27;weight&#x27;. Default: both &#x27;kv_cache&#x27; and &#x27;weight&#x27;. Example: --offload-rollout-level kv_cache weight |
| offload_train_target | --offload-train-target | str | [&quot;cpu&quot;, &quot;disk&quot;] | &quot;cpu&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Where the training actor is backed up while offloaded during rollout (only used with --offload-train on the megatron backend). &#x27;cpu&#x27; (default) keeps a pinned host copy; &#x27;disk&#x27; streams it to node-local NVMe (--offload-train-disk-dir) for the case where even CPU RAM cannot hold it. |
| stream_optimizer_state_to_disk | --stream-optimizer-state-to-disk | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Stream the fp32 main params and Adam moments through per-bucket files on node-local NVMe during optimizer.step(), bounding GPU residency to one bucket. For when the optimizer state does not fit the GPU *while the step runs*: --offload-train-target=disk cannot help there, because pause/resume happen at phase boundaries and everything is resident again by the time Adam launches. Bit-identical to keeping the state on GPU, at the cost of disk traffic every step. Distinct from --offload-optimizer-states and --optimizer-cpu-offload, and mutually exclusive with both. |
| stream_optimizer_state_moment_dtype | --stream-optimizer-state-moment-dtype | str | [&quot;bf16&quot;, &quot;fp16&quot;, &quot;fp32&quot;, &quot;fp8e4m3&quot;, &quot;fp8e5m2&quot;] | &quot;fp32&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | On-disk dtype for the streamed Adam moments; the fp32 master copy is always fp32. This is a serialization format, not a compute precision: the step still hands fp32 tensors to FusedAdam, and the cast happens on the way to and from disk. That makes it distinct from --exp-avg-dtype / --exp-avg-sq-dtype, which change what the optimizer holds and require --use-precision-aware-optimizer, so they cannot be combined with streaming at all. The step is I/O bound and the moments tolerate less precision than the master copy, so bf16 cuts streaming volume by a third (12 bytes per param to 8). fp32 is bit-identical to keeping the moments on GPU. The fp8 options need per-block scaling for exp_avg_sq to be sound, which this does not implement, and are not recommended. |
| offload_train_disk_dir | --offload-train-disk-dir | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Node-local directory for the disk-offload files, used by both --offload-train-target=disk and --stream-optimizer-state-to-disk (each under its own subdirectory). Should be fast local NVMe (e.g. /scratch); a tmpfs mount, which /tmp is on many systems, keeps the data in RAM and defeats both. Files are per-process and overwritten in place every step (bounded size); defaults to $SCRATCH/miles_train_offload_&lt;uid&gt;. |
| offload_train_disk_chunk_mb | --offload-train-disk-chunk-mb | int | — | 256 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Chunk size (MiB) for the GPU&lt;-&gt;disk transfers, i.e. the pinned host staging buffer, which bounds host memory regardless of how much is moved. Used by both --offload-train-target=disk and --stream-optimizer-state-to-disk, and each allocates its own, so enabling both costs 2x this per rank. |
| distributed_backend | --distributed-backend | str | — | &quot;nccl&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Distributed process-group backend requested by MILES runtime helpers. |
| distributed_timeout_minutes | --distributed-timeout-minutes | int | — | 10 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Distributed process-group timeout in minutes. |
| train_backend | --train-backend | str | [&quot;fsdp&quot;, &quot;megatron&quot;, &quot;olmo_core&quot;] | &quot;megatron&quot; | Adapter-owned; cannot override | The backend for training. |
| qkv_format | --qkv-format | str | [&quot;bshd&quot;, &quot;thd&quot;] | &quot;thd&quot; | thd with sequence_packing; bshd otherwise | The qkv layout. |
| linear_attention_backend | --linear-attention-backend | str | [&quot;fla&quot;, &quot;flashqla&quot;] | &quot;fla&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Backend for Qwen GDN linear-attention layers. &#x27;fla&#x27; (flash-linear-attention) is portable and runs on any supported GPU. &#x27;flashqla&#x27; (FlashQLA) requires NVIDIA SM90 (Hopper) or newer, CUDA 12.8+, and PyTorch 2.8+. |
| miles_dsa_topk_backend | --miles-dsa-topk-backend | str | [&quot;flashinfer&quot;, &quot;torch&quot;] | &quot;torch&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Top-k backend for Miles DSA indexer. |
| true_on_policy_mode | --true-on-policy-mode | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Whether to enable true-on-policy mode. |
| recompute_logprobs_via_prefill | --recompute-logprobs-via-prefill | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Recompute rollout logprobs via SGLang prefill instead of decode kernels. Only needed for models whose prefill and decode paths are not numerically identical. |
| train_env_vars | --train-env-vars | loads | — | &quot;{}&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Extra environment variables for training process, e.g. PyTorch memory management ones. |
| train_memory_margin_bytes | --train-memory-margin-bytes | int | — | 1073741824 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Add margin for train memory allocation. By default we will reserve 1GB as margin. |
| debug_skip_weight_update | --debug-skip-weight-update | switch | — | false | Required value: false | Debug-only: preserve the train/rollout offload-onload schedule, but skip the actual actor-to-rollout weight update. |
| debug_disable_optimizer | --debug-disable-optimizer | switch | — | false | Required value: false | Debug-only: do not initialize the Megatron optimizer or LR scheduler. Training still runs rollout, log-prob forward, and actor forward/backward, but skips optimizer state allocation and optimizer updates. |
| rematerialize_param_from_master_weight | --rematerialize-param-from-master-weight | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Colocate CPU memory optimization. Drop the actor&#x27;s parameter weight backup during inference, and rebuild it from the optimizer&#x27;s master weights on the next train step. Reduces peak CPU memory by 2*param per rank (bf16 training). Works with both the GPU optimizer and the CPU optimizer, but is not compatible with --use-precision-aware-optimizer on GPU. ref/teacher tags keep their backups. Recommended for Grace GPU colocate training. |
| check_rematerialize_param_from_master_weight | --check-rematerialize-param-from-master-weight | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Debug: SHA256-verify the first two rematerialize cycles are bit-identical. |
| megatron_to_hf_mode | --megatron-to-hf-mode | value | [&quot;bridge&quot;, &quot;raw&quot;] | &quot;raw&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The method to convert megatron weights to hugging face weights for SGLang. |
| dsa_attention_backend | --dsa-attention-backend | value | [&quot;megatron&quot;, &quot;tilelang&quot;] | &quot;tilelang&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | DSA sparse-MLA kernel backend for GLM (glm_moe_dsa) under --megatron-to-hf-mode bridge. &#x27;tilelang&#x27; (default) uses the fused TileLang kernels (SparseMLA + lighting_indexer, vendored from slime) for rollout&lt;-&gt;train numerical parity; &#x27;megatron&#x27; uses the portable unfused megatron-core kernels. &#x27;tilelang&#x27; requires --qkv-format thd and the optional tilelang dep, and is training/forward-only (no KV cache, cannot serve inference). Both support GLM-5.1 and GLM-5.2, full or LoRA. No effect on non-DSA models or the &#x27;raw&#x27; path. |
| extra_high_precision_layers_hf | --extra-high-precision-layers-hf | str | — | [] | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Extra substrings for HF weight names to skip quantization (e.g. .kv_b_proj.). |
| extra_high_precision_layers_megatron | --extra-high-precision-layers-megatron | str | — | [] | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Extra substrings for Megatron weight names to skip quantization in Megatron-to-HF paths (e.g. .linear_kv_up_proj.). |
| custom_model_provider_path | --custom-model-provider-path | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Path to a custom model provider function. If set, we will use this function instead of the default model provider. The function should have the signature `def custom_model_provider(pre_process: bool, post_process: bool, vp_stage: int &#124; None = None) -&gt; GPTModel`. Example: &#x27;my_module.my_model_provider&#x27;. |
| recompute_loss_function | --recompute-loss-function | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Whether to enable recompute loss function to save memory during training. |
| log_probs_chunk_size | --log-probs-chunk-size | int | — | -1 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Chunk size to compute log probs to save memory |
| indep_dp | --indep-dp | switch | — | false | Required value: false; no Core implementation | Launch each DP replica as an independent Megatron instance instead of using Megatron-internal data parallelism. |
| delay_split_train_data_by_dp | --delay-split-train-data-by-dp | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Inherited data-parallel split timing control; do not assume it changes Core sample partitioning. |
| allgather_cp | --allgather-cp | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Inherited context-parallel gather control; Core trainer CP must be one. |
| low_memory_resume | --low-memory-resume | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Allocate optimizer states on CPU during checkpoint loading to prevent GPU OOM on memory spike.  |
| mfu_peak_tflops | --mfu-peak-tflops | float | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Peak dense BF16 TFLOP/s of one training GPU — the denominator of perf/actor_train_mfu. Defaults to a built-in table keyed on the device name; set this for a device the table does not know, or to report MFU against another precision&#x27;s peak. With neither available the MFU metric is not logged. |
| hf_checkpoint | --hf-checkpoint | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The huggingface checkpoint of the trained model. This is used to initialize sglang and also provide the tokenizer. Note that, we will always update the parameters in sglang with that of megatron before training, so you only need to provide a huggingface checkpoint that has the same architecture as the model you want to train. It doesn&#x27;t necessary need to contain the most up-to-date parameters. |
| model_name | --model-name | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The name of the model, this is used to convert the megatron weights into huggingface format. If not set, we will use `type(load_hf_config(args.hf_checkpoint)).__name__.lower()` as model_name. Also, sometimes this will help alleviate the bug that transformers cannot find certain model. |
| rollout_function_path | --rollout-function-path | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Path to the rollout generation function. Use this to create your own custom rollout function and set this to its path. The function is called as `fn(args, rollout_id, data_source, evaluation=evaluation)`, so its signature should be `def generate_rollout(args, rollout_id, data_source, evaluation=False) -&gt; RolloutFnTrainOutput &#124; RolloutFnEvalOutput` (see `miles.rollout.inference_rollout.inference_rollout_common.InferenceRolloutFn` for the default class-based implementation). Within each output sample, set at least `tokens`, `response_length`, `reward`, and `truncated`. |
| fully_async | --fully-async | switch | — | false | Requires disaggregated resident engines and positive Core lag allowance | Run fully async rollout: a persistent worker keeps generating while the trainer drains completed groups. Selects `FullyAsyncRolloutFn` as the rollout function; evaluation keeps the standard rollout function, which fully async does not serve. Requires train_async.py. |
| rollout_temperature | --rollout-temperature | float | — | 1.0 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | the temperature for the inference engine during rollout. |
| rollout_top_p | --rollout-top-p | float | — | 1.0 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | the top-p for the inference engine during rollout. |
| rollout_top_k | --rollout-top-k | int | — | -1 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | the top-k for the inference engine during rollout. |
| rollout_max_context_len | --rollout-max-context-len | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The maximum context size for the inference engine during rollout.It should no exceed the `max_position_embeddinds` in Huggingface model&#x27;s `config.json` |
| rollout_max_prompt_len | --rollout-max-prompt-len | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The maximum length of the prompt for the inference engine during rollout. If set, we will filter out the long prompts during initialization of the global dataset. This is not recommended if the dataset is large. |
| rollout_max_response_len | --rollout-max-response-len | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The maximum length of the response for the inference engine during rollout. It is basically `max_tokens` in sglang. |
| rollout_skip_special_tokens | --rollout-skip-special-tokens | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Whether to skip special tokens in the response during rollout. This is useful when you want to use the response as a prompt for the next rollout. |
| rollout_stop | --rollout-stop | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The stop words for the inference engine during rollout. It can be a list of strings or a single string. It may be hard to pass special tokens in command line, in that case rollout_stop_token_ids can be used. |
| rollout_stop_token_ids | --rollout-stop-token-ids | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The stop token ids for the inference engine during rollout. It can be a list of integers or a single integer. |
| rollout_shuffle | --rollout-shuffle | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Whether to shuffle the prompts during rollout. |
| rollout_seed | --rollout-seed | int | — | 42 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | The seed for the random number generator during rollout. This is used to shuffle the prompts and also for the random sampling of the prompts. |
| object_store_backend | --object-store-backend | str | [&quot;mooncake&quot;, &quot;ray&quot;] | &quot;ray&quot; | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Backend of the object store used to pass data (e.g. rollout data) between processes. |
| mooncake_store_init_kwargs | --mooncake-store-init-kwargs | loads | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | JSON kwargs used to initialize MooncakeDistributedStore for rollout transfer. |
| mooncake_replica_num | --mooncake-replica-num | int | — | 1 | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Number of Mooncake memory replicas for each stored object. |
| over_sampling_batch_size | --over-sampling-batch-size | int | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | This defines the granularity of the sampling batch in the rollout function. When the number of available samples falls below the target, a sampling operation of size over_sampling_batch_size will be triggered.Regardless of whether partial rollout is used or filters are applied, the sampling granularity is always determined by this value. If this value is None, rollout_batch_size will be used as the default over_sampling_batch_size. |
| dynamic_sampling_filter_path | --dynamic-sampling-filter-path | str | — | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | This is the filter function for dynamic sampling. It should be able to judge whether the result of a prompt should be selected or not.We will do dynamic filter for sampling as in DAPO. e.g. not all correct or all wrong samples.You could use `miles.rollout.filter_hub.dynamic_sampling_filters.check_reward_nonzero_std` as an example. |
| rollout_submission_granularity | --rollout-submission-granularity | str | [&quot;group&quot;, &quot;sample&quot;] | null | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Granularity at which a completed unit frees rollout submission capacity. `group` holds a slot until the whole prompt group returns; `sample` frees each slot as its own sample finishes, so a replacement group goes out once n_samples_per_prompt samples complete, whichever groups they came from. Prompt groups are submitted whole either way. Unset picks the driver default: `sample` under --fully-async, where groups completed beyond the batch are queued for later steps; `group` otherwise, where they are aborted at the end of the step and, without --partial-rollout, discarded. |
| partial_rollout | --partial-rollout | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Whether to use partial rollout. If set, the unfinished samples during dynamic sampling will be recycled back to data buffer. This is useful for long responses. |
| mask_offpolicy_in_partial_rollout | --mask-offpolicy-in-partial-rollout | switch | — | false | Parser option; subject to Core/model/runtime validation | Whether to mask previous generation in partial rollout. If set, only on-policy generated tokens will be used in training |
| max_weight_staleness | --max-weight-staleness | int | — | null | Must equal core.max_policy_lag | Maximum allowed gap between a group&#x27;s oldest weight version and the current engine weight version. Groups exceeding this threshold are recycled back to the data buffer instead of being sent to training. Only effective in fully async mode. None (default) disables staleness filtering. |
